## PPC for Law Firms UK | Google Ads for Solicitors, One Consultant

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/ppc-for-law-firms/
Description: PPC for UK law firms: Google Ads by practice area, enquiries counted as instructions, research searches excluded, SRA rules respected. Flat fee.

Legal is one of the most expensive auctions in the UK. Employment, conveyancing, family and personal injury searches cost from several pounds to well over £15 a click in the large cities. At that price, the difference between a firm that profits from Google Ads and one that does not is almost never the bid. It is what gets counted, what gets excluded and the page after the click.

## Where law firm accounts waste money

- Research searches billed as leads. "How much does a divorce cost", "can I be sacked for", "free legal advice". These searches match broad and phrase keywords, cost as much as a client search, and almost never instruct. Twelve months of search terms read line by line is the first task.

- One campaign for the whole firm. Family, employment and conveyancing share a budget, and the cheapest enquiries take it. Each practice area gets its own campaign, budget and landing page.

- A call counted as a client. Phone clicks and form fills are not instructions. Call tracking tied to the keyword, a qualifying form and the case management system feeding back which enquiries became matters are what let Google optimise towards clients.

- The firm's homepage as the landing page. Someone who searched for an employment solicitor should land on a page about employment law, with the solicitor's name, the first-step explained and the phone number at the top.

- Adverts that would not pass compliance. Claims about outcomes, "no win no fee" without the qualifications, comparative claims about other firms. The SRA Transparency Rules and the ASA set what can be said, and the adverts are written inside that.

## What a click costs by practice area and city

Average cost per click from Google Ads keyword data for the UK, October 2026, for the search with the city attached. Market averages, not a forecast.

| Search | London | Manchester | Birmingham | Leeds | Bristol |

| solicitors [city] | £13.49 | £9.46 | £9.31 | £7.09 | £7.97 |

| employment lawyer [city] | £18.60 | £10.95 | £10.92 | £9.99 | £11.72 |

At these prices, 100 clicks on an employment search in London cost close to £1,900. If one in ten calls and one in four callers instructs, that is £760 per instruction before the fee. If a third of those clicks were research searches that should have been excluded, the real figure was closer to £500. That is the arithmetic the account is run on.

## What management includes for a law firm

- A campaign per practice area, with exact and phrase match, a negatives programme built from the research vocabulary of each area, and location targeting matched to where the firm takes clients.

- Measurement to the matter. Call tracking, a form that asks the qualifying question, and the case management system (Clio, LEAP, Proclaim or a spreadsheet) feeding back which enquiries opened a file, imported to Google Ads as offline conversions. See conversion tracking.

- A page per practice area, built by me, with the solicitor, the process, the fee basis as the Transparency Rules require, and a phone number and form that work on a mobile at lunchtime. See landing pages.

- Brand and competitor terms decided, not defaulted. Whether to bid on the firm's own name depends on who else is bidding on it; competitor bidding is legal in the UK and usually poor value. Both reviewed monthly.

- Microsoft Advertising once Google works: a professional audience on work devices, often at a lower cost per enquiry for legal searches. Microsoft Ads →

- A monthly report in instructions and cost per instruction, by practice area, alongside the platform numbers so the two can be compared.

## Who this fits

UK firms from a few fee earners to mid-size regional practices, spending roughly £2,000 to £40,000 a month, in practice areas where a client is worth several hundred pounds or more: employment, family, private client, conveyancing, commercial, immigration, personal injury where the firm handles its own intake. Claims management companies and lead resellers are not a fit. There is no law firm case on this site yet and none will be invented; the published cases show the method on other expensive auctions.

### FAQ

**How much should a law firm spend on Google Ads?** Enough to buy a meaningful number of clicks in your practice area and city, which the table above lets you estimate: at £10 to £19 a click, a few thousand pounds a month is the floor for a single practice area in a large city. The first call includes this arithmetic for your firm.

**Can you work within SRA and ASA rules?** Yes. Adverts avoid outcome claims and comparative claims, 'no win no fee' carries its qualifications, and the landing pages carry the price and service information the SRA Transparency Rules require for the relevant areas. Your compliance partner signs off the copy before it runs.

**Do you bid on competitor firm names?** Only if the numbers support it, and they usually do not: the clicks are expensive, the conversion rate is low and the ASA has rules on how the advert may be worded. It is reviewed, not assumed.

**Can you connect Google Ads to our case management system?** Yes, through an offline conversion import: Clio, LEAP, Proclaim and most systems can export the enquiries that became matters, and a scheduled upload teaches Google which clicks produced clients.

**How much does PPC management for a law firm cost?** A flat monthly fee set from the scope: practice areas, platforms and how much landing page and tracking work is included. Never a percentage of spend. Quoted in pounds, ex VAT, by email from the form. See pricing.

## Healthcare PPC and Digital Marketing UK | Clinics and Health Brands

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/healthcare-ppc/
Description: Healthcare PPC and paid digital marketing for UK private clinics, dental practices and health brands, by one consultant instead of a healthcare marketing agency.

Private healthcare is a crowded UK auction with its own constraints: restricted remarketing, certification for some categories, claims the ASA and the CAP Code do not allow, and patients who research for weeks before booking. The accounts that work are the ones where the measurement reaches the appointment book and the campaigns respect the research journey instead of paying for it twice.

## What is different about healthcare accounts

- Policy limits the tools. Google restricts personalised advertising for health conditions, so remarketing lists built on condition pages are not available; some categories (prescription medicines, certain treatments) require certification before adverts run; Meta has its own health and wellness data restrictions. The structure has to work without the tools other sectors lean on.

- Claims are regulated. Outcome claims, before-and-after imagery for some procedures, and anything that implies a guarantee fall under the CAP Code and, for medicines and devices, the MHRA. Copy is written inside those rules and your clinical lead signs it off.

- Research searches dominate. "Symptoms of", "is it normal", "NHS waiting time for" are expensive, well-meaning and do not book. They are excluded, and the budget goes to the searches that name a treatment, a clinic or a location.

- The conversion is an appointment, not a form. Reception answers the phone; the booking system knows who attended. Until those feed back, Google optimises towards whoever fills in a form, including the people who never show up.

## What management includes

- Structure by treatment and location. A campaign per service line (implants, cosmetic, physiotherapy, fertility, diagnostics) with location targeting matched to how far patients travel for that treatment, and the research vocabulary excluded.

- Measurement to the appointment. Call tracking with reception outcomes, booking system or practice management software (Dentally, Cliniko, Semble and others) feeding attended appointments back as offline conversions, Consent Mode v2 and a privacy setup that keeps health data out of the ad platforms. See conversion tracking.

- Pages built for a worried person. One page per treatment with the clinician, the process, the price basis, the next available appointment and a phone number at the top, loading fast on a mobile. See landing pages.

- Meta where it fits. Awareness and remarketing for elective treatments, within Meta's health restrictions, judged on booked consultations rather than on form fills. Facebook Ads →

- Reporting in appointments. Cost per booked and attended appointment by treatment, alongside the platform numbers, in pounds.

## Looking for a healthcare digital marketing agency?

Clinics and health brands that search for a healthcare digital marketing agency usually want one of two things: more patients from the adverts they already pay for, or a plan for where to advertise at all. Both are covered here for the paid side of digital marketing: Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising and Meta, the treatment pages the adverts lead to, and the measurement back to the appointment book.

The difference from an agency is who does the work. There is no account team. The consultant who reads your account is the one who writes the adverts, builds the pages and reports each month. What is left to others is said plainly: search engine optimisation, organic social media and PR are not part of this practice, and a group that needs all of them under one roof is better served by a full-service healthcare marketing agency.

## Who this fits

UK private clinics and groups, dental practices, physiotherapy and diagnostics providers, aesthetics clinics working within the rules, and health brands selling direct. Typically £2,000 to £40,000 a month across Google and Meta. Past roles include senior in-house paid media work in healthcare and a freelance role with a US pharmaceutical agency; no patient-facing UK case is published on this site, and none will be invented.

## Healthcare marketing research and guides from Diwizi

Diwizi is the same practice organised by sector, and it publishes the longer research. For healthcare:

### The State of Healthcare Marketing 2027

A free Diwizi Research report on how people find care, how the pandemic rerouted it and how AI is entering discovery, diagnosis and the hospital ward.

### Why healthcare ad costs run high and what policy changes

Google Ads for hospitals, clinics and B2B pharma, with the compliance limits and benchmark data from the US, the UK and Brazil.

New patient acquisition sized to what the practice can actually see in a week.

High-value treatments, call tracking and the real cost of acquiring a patient.

For medtech, health software and companies selling into hospitals and health systems.

Paid media organised by service line rather than by institution.

Most of this material is written for an international readership and leans on US examples. For a UK clinic, the rules described on this page are the ones that apply: the CAP Code, the MHRA and the health policies of Google and Meta.

### FAQ

**Can you run Google Ads for a private clinic given the health policies?** Yes. The restrictions remove some tools (condition-based remarketing, some audience features) and require certification for certain categories. The account is built to work within that, and the certification process is handled with you where it applies.

**Can you connect Google Ads to our booking system?** Usually, through an offline conversion import: Dentally, Cliniko, Semble and most practice systems can export which enquiries booked and attended, without sending any clinical data to Google. Where there is no export, reception outcomes from call tracking do most of the job.

**What about GDPR and patient data?** No health data goes to the ad platforms. Conversions are sent as outcomes (booked, attended) with hashed contact data where enhanced conversions are used, under Consent Mode v2, and the setup is documented for your data protection lead.

**Are you a healthcare digital marketing agency?** No. This is an independent practice with one senior consultant, covering the paid side of healthcare digital marketing: Google, Microsoft and Meta Ads, treatment landing pages and measurement to the booked appointment. Search engine optimisation, organic social media and PR are left to others.

**Do you work with dental practices?** Yes. Dental is one of the more competitive local health auctions in the UK, and the structure by treatment (implants, Invisalign, emergency, general) with the practice management system feeding back attended appointments is the pattern that works.

**How much does healthcare PPC management cost?** A flat monthly fee set from the scope: treatments, locations, platforms and how much landing page and tracking work is included. Never a percentage of spend. Quoted in pounds, ex VAT, by email from the form. See pricing.

## SaaS PPC Consultant UK | Google Ads Measured in Pipeline

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/saas-ppc/
Description: SaaS PPC for UK and Irish software companies: Google Ads connected to the CRM and reported in pipeline and CAC payback. Flat fee.

Software companies have the cleanest data in paid media and often the worst use of it. The CRM knows which trials became customers and what they pay; the ad platforms are optimising towards sign-ups. Connecting the two is most of the job, and it is where a SaaS account starts here.

## Where SaaS accounts leak

- Optimising towards the top of the funnel. Free trials, demo requests and content downloads are easy to count and cheap to buy. Without product-qualified or sales-accepted stages flowing back, the platforms buy the cheapest sign-ups, which churn.

- Competitor and category terms treated the same. "[Competitor] alternative" and "best [category] software" bring different buyers at different stages and should sit in separate campaigns with separate pages and expectations.

- Brand taking the credit. Performance Max and broad match drift onto the brand name and the reported CAC looks wonderful. Brand is isolated, and the non-brand number is the one managed.

- Payback ignored. A customer acquired at £900 on a £40 monthly plan is a 22-month payback before gross margin. The targets by plan and segment come from that arithmetic, not from a blended CAC.

## What management includes

- Measurement to the CRM. GA4 and Tag Manager with a user ID, HubSpot or Salesforce stages (MQL, SQL, opportunity, closed won, with amount) imported to Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising as offline conversions, so the platforms optimise towards revenue. See conversion tracking.

- Google Search by intent. Category, problem, integration and competitor campaigns, each with its own page and its own target, brand kept separate, Performance Max only with brand excluded and only once the conversion data deserves it.

- Microsoft Advertising for the professional audience on work devices, with LinkedIn profile bid adjustments Google cannot offer. Microsoft Ads →

- Pages per intent, built by me: comparison pages, integration pages, use-case pages, with the trial or demo form that asks the one qualifying question. See landing pages.

- Reporting in pipeline and payback. Qualified pipeline, closed-won revenue and CAC payback by channel and segment, alongside the platform numbers.

## A published SaaS result

At Pontomais, a time-tracking and HR software company in Brazil, I rebuilt the Google Ads account as an employee. Contact requests from Google Ads went from about five in a month to the hundreds over eight months, approximate volumes from my own experience on the project, and the full note is on results. The market was Brazil and the currency was different, but the method was the one above: the account rebuilt around buying intent, landing page changes, and daily feedback from sales on the quality of each contact.

## Who this fits

UK and Irish B2B software companies from seed to Series B, or established vertical SaaS, spending roughly £3,000 to £60,000 a month on Google and Microsoft, with a CRM in use and a sales or product-led motion that can report stages. Consumer apps measured on installs are not a fit.

### FAQ

**What CAC should a SaaS company expect from Google Ads?** No honest number exists before the account and the CRM are read together. What is measurable from the first month is CAC by channel and segment against your plan prices, which gives payback, and that is the figure the targets are set from.

**Can you connect Google Ads to HubSpot or Salesforce?** Yes. Offline conversion import from CRM stages with amounts, enhanced conversions for leads, and a user ID in GA4 so the journey from click to closed won is visible. The setup is documented so your RevOps team owns it.

**Should we bid on competitor names?** Usually yes, in a separate campaign with its own page and a target that reflects the lower conversion rate. Comparison pages that are honest about where the competitor is better convert well and stay within the advertising rules.

**Do you run product-led growth accounts?** Yes, provided product-qualified signals (activation, team invites, usage thresholds) can be fed back. Without them the platforms optimise towards sign-ups that never activate, and the budget is better spent elsewhere.

**How much does SaaS PPC management cost?** A flat monthly fee set from the scope: platforms, markets, campaigns and how much landing page and tracking work is included. Never a percentage of spend. Quoted in pounds, ex VAT, by email from the form. See pricing.

## What Manchester accounts usually need

Manchester is the second paid search market in the UK by most measures, with a professional services, technology and property base that competes on the same searches as London at a lower price per click. The margin for error is wider than in London; the habits that waste budget are the same.

- Location targeting that matches how you actually serve. A radius around the office for the work that needs a visit, the wider region for the work that does not, and the two bid separately instead of one pin on the city centre.

- Enquiry quality over enquiry count. Call tracking tied to the keyword, form fields that qualify, and CRM stages fed back to Google and Microsoft so bidding learns from clients, not from clicks.

- A landing page per intent. Not the homepage, and not one generic contact page for twelve services.

- Brand and competitor terms handled deliberately. Whether to bid on your own name depends on who else is bidding on it in Manchester this month, and the answer changes.

Average cost per click for the same search with the city name attached, from Google Ads keyword data for the UK, October 2026. Market averages, not a forecast for your account.

There is no Manchester case study on this site yet, and none will be invented. What can be shown is the order of work I use in home services accounts, including a Houston HVAC and plumbing engagement whose figures are confidential by contract. None of it is a bidding trick:

- Campaigns split by type of job, so urgent, cheaper work does not absorb the budget meant for higher-value jobs.

## PPC Consultation UK | One-Off Google Ads Session With Written Notes

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/ppc-consultation/
Description: Book a PPC consultation: one working session on your account with a senior consultant on UK hours, written notes afterwards. Fixed price in pounds.

Not every account needs an audit or a retainer. Sometimes a business needs a senior person to look at the account for an hour, answer the three questions that have been going round for months, and write down what to do next. That is the consultation, and it is the smallest way to work with me.

## When a consultation is the right size

- A decision is pending. Whether to move to Performance Max, whether to take the agency's proposal, whether the budget increase is justified, whether to bid on the brand. A second opinion from someone with no retainer to win.

- An in-house marketer wants a senior check. You run the account yourself and want an experienced pair of eyes on the structure, the tracking and the search terms before the next quarter.

- Something broke. Conversions stopped recording, the account was suspended, spend doubled overnight, and you need the cause and the fix without a six-week engagement.

- You are choosing a supplier. You have two agency proposals and want them read by someone who runs accounts, with the questions to ask each one.

## How the consultation works

- Before the call. You send the form with the spend band, the platforms and the questions. If the account is live, read-only access to Google Ads and GA4 so the hour is spent on answers rather than on screen-sharing.

- The session. A video call of about an hour, on UK time, working through the account and your questions in order of money at stake. Recorded if you want it.

- Written notes within two working days. What was found, what to do, in what order, and what to measure to know it worked. Written so your team or your agency can act on it.

- Credited if it grows. If the consultation becomes a full audit or management within 60 days, the consultation fee is credited against it.

If one session is not enough, the PPC consultancy can take the account on as an ongoing engagement.

## Consultation, audit or management

| | Consultation | Audit | Management |

| What it is | One working session plus notes | A full written review of every platform in scope | Running the account month to month |

| Time | About an hour, notes within two working days | 5 to 7 working days | Ongoing, 30 days' notice either way |

| Best for | A decision, a second opinion, a broken thing, an in-house check | Knowing everything that is wrong and what it costs | Having the senior person do the work |

| Price | Fixed, in pounds, quoted from the form | Fixed, set from spend, campaigns and platforms | Flat monthly fee, set from scope |

| Credited against | An audit or management within 60 days | The first month of management | |

How each is priced, with market ranges, is on pricing.

## What a consultation is not

It is not a sales call dressed as advice: the fee is the same whether or not you go on to work with me, and most consultations end with the notes. It is not a free audit; those are on the audit page, with the reasons they are a poor idea. And it is not training in Google Ads from the ground up; it assumes someone on your side runs or oversees the account already.

### FAQ

**How much does a PPC consultation cost?** A fixed fee in pounds, ex VAT, quoted by email from the form within one working day. It is credited against an audit or the first month of management if either follows within 60 days. See pricing for how everything is priced.

**Can we book more than one session?** Yes. Some in-house teams book a session each month or each quarter as a standing review; that is agreed in writing after the first one, with the same notes each time.

**Do you need access to our account for a consultation?** It helps: read-only access to Google Ads and GA4 beforehand means the hour goes on answers. Without access, the session works from your screen share and your questions, and the notes say what to check.

**Which platforms can the consultation cover?** Google Ads (Search, Shopping, Performance Max, YouTube, Demand Gen), Microsoft Advertising and Meta Ads, plus GA4, Tag Manager and landing pages.

**Is the consultation available to businesses outside the UK?** Yes. UK businesses are quoted in pounds here and Irish businesses in euros; businesses in the US, Canada and the rest of Europe have the same session on googleadsfreelancer.com, quoted in dollars, pounds or euros.

## Performance Marketing Agency Alternative UK | One Senior Consultant

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/performance-marketing/
Description: Looking for a performance marketing agency in the UK? Paid search, shopping and paid social judged on enquiries and sales, run by one senior consultant.

Performance marketing is the part of marketing you can hold to a number: what an enquiry, a sale or a new customer cost, and whether that was worth paying. UK businesses usually look for a performance marketing agency to run it. This is the same work done by one consultant with 14+ years on the account, across Google, Microsoft and Meta Ads, with the landing pages and the measurement handled by the same person.

## What performance marketing means when you are the one paying

The label covers any advertising that is bought and judged on a measurable outcome rather than on reach. In practice, for most UK businesses, it comes down to four things done together.

### Paid search

Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising on the searches people make when they are ready to buy or enquire. Where most performance budgets should start. Google Ads → Microsoft Ads →

### Shopping and Performance Max

Product listings and Google's automated campaigns for online stores, judged on margin and new customers instead of on the platform's own revenue figure. E-commerce PPC →

### Paid social

Meta Ads on Facebook and Instagram for demand that search cannot reach, with remarketing and creative tested against a control. Facebook Ads →

### Measurement and pages

Conversion tracking that reaches the enquiry or the order, and a landing page for each intent. Without these two, the rest is only spend. Tracking → Landing pages →

## The numbers that make it performance

- Cost per qualified enquiry, not cost per lead. A form filled in by a student and one filled in by a buyer are the same lead on a dashboard. The report separates them, using what your sales team or your CRM says happened next.

- Return measured on margin. For a store, revenue reported by the ad platform is reconciled against the orders in the store itself, with returns and product margin taken into account.

- New customers shown apart from existing ones. Brand searches and remarketing flatter every account. They are reported in their own line so the cost of winning a new customer is visible.

- Payback over the real sales cycle. A B2B enquiry that closes in ninety days is judged over ninety days, by cohort, not against the month it arrived in.

These numbers depend on measurement that works under UK consent rules: Consent Mode v2, enhanced conversions and, where there is a sales team, offline conversions imported from the CRM. That work is part of the engagement, not an extra.

## Performance marketing agency or independent consultant

| | Independent consultant | Performance marketing agency |

| Who works on the account | The person you first spoke to, every week | An account team, usually led day to day by someone other than the person who pitched |

| Channels | Google, Microsoft and Meta Ads, with tracking and landing pages | Often wider: affiliates, influencers, programmatic display, marketplaces |

| What is reported | Cost per qualified enquiry or sale, reconciled to your CRM or your orders | Varies. Ask whether the figures are the platform's or yours |

| Suits | One business spending roughly £2,000 to £60,000 a month on paid media | Many markets or languages, heavy creative production, or channels listed above |

If your plan depends on an affiliate programme, influencer work or programmatic buying at scale, an agency is the right choice and I will say so on the first call. The longer comparison is on PPC agency vs PPC consultant.

### FAQ

**What is a performance marketing agency?** An agency that runs advertising bought and judged on measurable outcomes, such as enquiries, sales or new customers, rather than on reach or awareness. The channels are usually paid search, shopping, paid social and sometimes affiliates or programmatic display.

**Are you a performance marketing agency?** No. This is an independent practice with one senior consultant. The work is the same as the paid search, shopping and paid social side of a performance marketing agency, done by the person you speak to, without an account team in between.

**Which channels do you cover?** Google Ads (Search, Shopping, Performance Max, YouTube and Demand Gen), Microsoft Advertising and Meta Ads, with GA4, Tag Manager, Consent Mode v2 and the landing pages that sit under them.

**Do you run affiliate, influencer or programmatic campaigns?** No. Those are separate disciplines, and a business that needs them at scale is better served by an agency or a specialist in that channel. I will tell you so before any work starts.

**How is performance measured?** On what your business counts: qualified enquiries, booked appointments, orders at their real margin, or pipeline from the CRM. Platform figures are shown next to those numbers, never in place of them.

## Lead Generation UK | B2B Lead Generation Through Paid Search

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/lead-generation/
Description: Lead generation for UK businesses through Google and Microsoft Ads: enquiries on your own website, tracked to the sale. An alternative to a lead generation agency.

A UK business looking for a lead generation agency or company usually finds two very different things under the same name. One sells you leads, often the same lead sold to several buyers. The other builds a flow of enquiries that arrive on your own website and belong to you. This page is about the second, run through Google, Microsoft and Meta Ads by one consultant.

## Two things sold as lead generation in the UK

| | Leads bought from a supplier | Enquiries from your own campaigns |

| Where the lead comes from | The supplier's forms, lists or call centre | A person who searched, saw your advert and filled in your form or rang your number |

| Who else gets it | Often several buyers, unless you pay for exclusivity | Only you |

| What you learn | Little. The supplier keeps the data on what worked | Which searches, adverts and pages bring customers, in your own accounts |

| What stays when you stop | Nothing | The accounts, the tracking, the landing pages and the history |

| Contact rules | You must be able to show the people on a bought list agreed to be contacted | The person asked you to get in touch about that request |

The last row matters more than most buyers realise. The government's guidance on direct marketing says that if you buy or rent a mailing list you should ask the supplier whether you have the right to use it for email marketing, and that it is illegal to phone someone registered with the Telephone Preference Service without their permission. An enquiry that came to you directly does not carry that risk.

## Lead generation companies in the UK, by what they sell

Disclosure. PPC Consultancy publishes this page and is on it. It is not in the table, because it sells one thing only: enquiries from your own paid campaigns. Every other company is in alphabetical order, described with facts read on its own website on 13 November 2026. None of them paid to be here or was contacted. If something has changed, a correction can be requested through the form.

The words lead generation cover very different services. The table sorts ten UK companies by what their own websites say they sell, so you can tell which kind you are talking to. The order is alphabetical and is not a ranking.

| Company | What its website says it sells | Kind |
| Achieve UK | B2B telemarketing and appointment setting for small businesses. Established in 1998. | Telephone |
| B2B Sales Leads | B2B lead generation and appointment setting, prospect data and outsourced sales development. | Telephone and data |
| Beach Marketing | B2B marketing for industrial brands with long buying cycles. Operating since 2008. | Agency |
| Beanstalk Marketing | B2B telemarketing and lead generation campaigns. Operating since 2009. | Telephone |
| Catalyst Marketing Agency | Digital marketing and lead generation for small and medium-sized businesses. Offices in Birmingham and London. | Agency |
| Choose Leads | B2C and B2B marketing data for telemarketing, email, postal and SMS campaigns. | Data |
| Leadly | Lead generation, SEO, PPC, CRM, creative and out of home. Based in Manchester. | Agency |
| Smartlead Marketing | B2B telemarketing and lead generation. | Telephone |
| The Lead Generation Agency | B2B lead generation through outreach, SEO and paid search. Based in London, operating since 2016. | Outreach and paid search |
| Toucan Telemarketing | Telemarketing and B2B appointment setting. Based in Cheshire, near Manchester. | Telephone |
Telephone means people calling prospects on your behalf to book appointments. Data means contact lists you then use yourself. Agency means marketing campaigns that bring enquiries to you. Before you sign with any of them, ask where each lead comes from, whether it is sold to anyone else, and how the people on a list agreed to be contacted.

## How lead generation through paid search is run here

- Search first. Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising on the searches that name the service, the problem or a competitor. Research searches and job seekers are excluded from the start.

- A page for each offer. Not the homepage. One page for the quote, one for the demo, one for the callback, each written to the advert that sends the visitor. See landing pages.

- Every enquiry counted, calls included. Forms, phone calls and bookings tracked under Consent Mode v2, so the cost per enquiry is a real figure. See conversion tracking.

- The outcome fed back. Which enquiries became quotes, opportunities and customers goes back to the ad platforms from your CRM, so the bidding learns from customers and not from form fills.

- Reporting in qualified enquiries. The monthly report shows the cost of an enquiry your sales team accepted, by campaign, next to the platform numbers.

## What an enquiry should cost

The arithmetic is short. The cost of an enquiry is the cost of a click divided by the share of visitors who enquire. If a click costs £6 and one visitor in twenty enquires, an enquiry costs £120. Halve the click price or double the share who enquire and the result is the same, which is why the landing page deserves as much attention as the bids.

Whether £120 is cheap depends on what a customer is worth to you and how many enquiries become customers. Those two numbers come from your business, not from the ad account. Click prices by sector, read from Google's own planning data for the United Kingdom, are in the guide to what Google Ads costs in the UK.

## A published example

For a reseller of health plans in Brazil, every campaign had one goal: a quote request submitted on the website. In October 2019, on almost the same spend as September, Google Ads produced 651 quote requests against 566, and the cost per request fell from R$ 16.42 to R$ 14.31.

Two months side by side from the report prepared at the time, not a trend. A quote request is a form submitted, not a plan sold. The case and its limits are on the results page.

## Who this fits

UK and Irish businesses that sell through enquiries, quotes, demos or booked calls: B2B and software companies, professional services, healthcare providers, and home and trade services. For a sales cycle measured in months, see B2B PPC and SaaS PPC. For regulated sectors, see PPC for law firms and healthcare PPC.

It does not fit a business that wants a fixed number of leads delivered each month for a price per lead. That is the bought-lead model, and it is not what is offered here.

### FAQ

**Do you sell leads?** No. I run the advertising, the tracking and the landing pages in your own accounts, and the enquiries arrive on your own website. You are not sharing them with another buyer, and the accounts stay with you if the work stops.

**Is this a lead generation agency?** No. It is an independent practice with one senior consultant. The work covers what a lead generation agency does through paid search and paid social, without an account team between you and the person doing it.

**How does B2B lead generation differ from consumer lead generation?** The sales cycle. A B2B enquiry may take months to become a customer, so the stages recorded in your CRM are sent back to Google and Microsoft, and results are judged by cohort over the real cycle instead of month by month.

**How soon do enquiries arrive?** Search adverts can show as soon as the campaigns are approved. Judging the cost of a qualified enquiry takes longer, because it depends on how long your sales team needs to accept or reject each one.

**Can I add the people who enquire to my marketing list?** An enquiry is a request to be contacted about that matter. Sending marketing emails or texts beyond it is covered by separate rules, which the Information Commissioner's Office sets out in its guidance on electronic mail marketing.

## Marketing Consultant UK | Digital Marketing Consultant for Paid Media

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/marketing-consultant/
Description: Independent digital marketing consultant for UK businesses: paid search, paid social, landing pages and measurement by one senior consultant with 14+ years.

Marketing consultant is a wide title. Some plan brands, some write content, some run events. I am Diego Willian Zietek, and for 14+ years my part has been paid media: Google, Microsoft and Meta Ads, the landing pages they send people to and the measurement that shows what the money brought back. If that is the part of your marketing that is costing you and not answering, this is the right page.

## What this marketing consultant does, and what is left to others

### In scope

- Google Ads: Search, Shopping, Performance Max, YouTube and Demand Gen

- Microsoft Advertising and Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram)

- Landing pages written and built for each advert

- GA4, Tag Manager, Consent Mode v2 and conversions imported from your CRM

- A paid media plan: which channels, in what order and on what budget

- Reviews of work done by your team or your agency

### Out of scope

- Search engine optimisation as an ongoing service

- Organic social media management and content calendars

- Public relations and events

- Email marketing programmes
If one of these is what your business needs first, I will say so on the first call instead of selling you adverts.

## When the marketing consultant you need is a paid media one

- You pay for adverts and cannot say which enquiries they brought. The reports show clicks and impressions, and the phone rings, but nobody can connect the two.

- The agency report arrives monthly and nothing changes. You want someone independent to read the account and tell you in writing what is wrong. That is the PPC audit.

- You are about to start advertising and do not want to learn on your own budget. A plan first: where to start, what it is likely to cost and what to measure. The guides on how to advertise your business in the UK and what Google Ads costs in the UK are a free starting point.

- Your team runs the accounts and wants a senior second opinion. A working session on a specific question, with a written note afterwards. See PPC consultation.

- You want one person to run it. The same consultant in the account every week, pages and tracking included. See PPC management.

## How the first weeks go

- A read of what exists. Read-only access to the ad accounts and analytics, and a look at the pages the adverts lead to.

- The measurement, before anything else. What counts as an enquiry or a sale, whether it is being counted once, and whether the consent banner is hiding results that did happen.

- A written plan. Which campaigns stay, which stop, what the budget should do and what a realistic cost per enquiry looks like for your sector.

- The work itself. Campaigns rebuilt where needed, a landing page for each main offer, and a report each month written for the person paying.

## Consultant, agency or a marketing hire

A marketing agency gives you a team and a wider range of services, with an account manager between you and the people doing the work. A marketing hire gives you one person on your payroll, who is rarely senior in every channel. An independent consultant gives you one senior person for a defined part of the job. For paid media in a business spending roughly £2,000 to £60,000 a month, that is usually enough, and the comparison is set out on PPC agency vs PPC consultant.

Fees are quoted in pounds, ex VAT, or in euros for Irish businesses, from the form. The pricing page explains how they are set.

### FAQ

**What does a digital marketing consultant do?** It depends on the consultant. The title covers strategy, search engine optimisation, content, social media, email and paid advertising. This practice covers paid advertising on Google, Microsoft and Meta, with the landing pages and the measurement, and says plainly when a business needs something else first.

**Do you do SEO or social media management?** No. Landing pages are built to convert paid traffic, and the tracking shows what organic search brings, but ongoing search engine optimisation and organic social media management are left to specialists in those fields.

**Do I need a marketing consultant or a PPC consultant?** If the question is which channels the business should use at all, a general marketing consultant is the right first call. If you already advertise, or have decided to, and the question is how to make that spend answer, a paid media consultant is the more direct route.

**Can you work alongside our marketing manager or agency?** Yes. Common arrangements are an independent audit of the paid accounts, a regular review of the work your team or agency does, or taking on the paid channels while your team keeps the rest.

**Where are you based?** In Curitiba, Brazil, three to four hours behind London. Most of the work is done in writing, calls are booked ahead and usually held in the UK afternoon, and everything is in English.

## How to choose an independent consultant

- Ask for a written review first. A consultant can read your account with read-only access and tell you in writing what is wrong before any ongoing work is agreed.

- Check the fit by sector. Several people on this list say on their own sites which kinds of business they work with. Believe them.

- Ask what happens when they are away. One person means one diary. A good answer is specific.

- Keep the accounts in your name. Whoever you choose, Google Ads, GA4 and Tag Manager belong to your business.

If your account needs several markets, heavy creative production or a team in the room, an agency is the better choice. Nine are listed on PPC agencies in the UK, and the difference between the two models is on PPC agency vs PPC consultant.

### FAQ

**Can I be added or removed?** Yes. Use the form on this site. Additions need a website that shows who does the work and that PPC is the main service.

**Should I choose a consultant near me?** It rarely matters for the work itself, which is done in the accounts and in writing. It matters if you want meetings in person, and in that case choose someone within reach.

## What 230 UK Businesses Paying for Google Ads Measure, by Sector

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/guides/google-ads-advertisers-measurement-uk/
Description: We read the sites of 230 UK businesses with live Google Ads in 15 service sectors. 43% show a Google Ads conversion tag. 14% show no measurement at all.

Of 230 UK businesses with live Google Ads in 15 service sectors, 43% show a Google Ads conversion tag on their site, 21% count visits with Google Analytics and show no Google Ads tag at all, and 14% show no measurement of any kind. Four in five publish a clickable phone number, and just over half of those have nothing in place to count the call. These companies are paying for clicks today. A large share cannot tell which click became a customer.

## The short version

43%show a Google Ads conversion tag on the home page or inside the tag container
21%count visits with Google Analytics and show no Google Ads tag at all
14%show no measurement of any kind
53%of the sites with a clickable phone number have nothing we could find to count the call

All 230 businesses had a Google ad shown in the United Kingdom between 23 October and 13 November 2026, according to Google's own Ads Transparency Center, and all of them are marked there as verified advertisers. They are paying for clicks now. Fewer than half show Google which click became a customer.

The figures are free to quote with a link to this page. The table by sector can be downloaded as a CSV file.

## Six groups, adding up to 100%

Every site falls into exactly one group, read from the outside, with no access to anyone's account.

| Group | Share of the 230 sites | What it means for the owner |

| A Google Ads conversion tag is visible | 43% | Google Ads is being told about at least one kind of result. Whether it is the right result is a separate question. |

| A Google Ads tag, but no conversion action visible from the home page | 13% | The tag is installed. The conversion may fire on a thank-you page we did not read, or may not exist. |

| Google Analytics or a Google tag, and no Google Ads tag | 21% | Visits are counted. Unless results are imported from Analytics into Google Ads, which cannot be seen from outside, the bidding learns nothing from enquiries. |

| Other tags only | 6% | An empty Tag Manager container, a retired Universal Analytics tag, a Meta Pixel or a heatmap tool, with nothing for Google Ads. |

| Signs of a tag we could not read | 3% | The page prepares for a Google tag but the ID is loaded by a script. Counted apart so the next row is not overstated. |

| No measurement of any kind | 14% | No Tag Manager, no Google tag, no Analytics, no Meta Pixel. The adverts run and nothing on the site records what they bring. |

## The phone call is the lead, and half the time nothing counts it

80% of the sites publish a phone number a visitor can tap. For most of these businesses the call is the enquiry they want. Among the 185 sites with a clickable number:

- 18% carry Google's own website call conversion, which swaps the number on the page for a Google forwarding number.

- 5% carry a call tracking service from another supplier.

- 37% have a tag that fires when the number is clicked, which counts taps and not conversations.

- 53% have none of the three.

One caveat matters here. Google's help page on conversion measurement says "Some kinds of conversion measurement don't require a tag", and gives the example of calls from call assets, where "you use a Google forwarding number to track when the call came from one of your ads". A business can therefore count calls made straight from the advert with nothing on its site. What it cannot count that way is the visitor who clicks the advert, reads the page and then rings the number on it.

## What the 230 sites carry

| What we looked for | Share of the 230 sites | Why it matters to the owner |

| Any Google Ads tag | 57% | The starting point for conversions and for remarketing |

| Google Ads conversion tag | 43% | Without it the account bids on clicks, not on enquiries |

| Google Analytics 4 or a Google tag | 69% | Visits are counted. Visits are not leads |

| Google Tag Manager container | 58% | The usual place the conversion tag lives |

| Meta Pixel | 16% | Facebook and Instagram adverts without it run blind |

| Microsoft Advertising tag | 8% | Few of these advertisers measure Bing at all |

| Consent banner from a recognisable tool | 40% | UK rules ask for a choice before marketing cookies are set |

| Clickable phone number | 80% | The enquiry most of these businesses actually want |

| Enquiry form on the home page | 53% | The other enquiry, and the easier one to count |

## One well-measured site in each sector

These sites carry the full set on their home page: a Google Ads conversion tag, some form of call measurement, Google Analytics and a consent banner. They are listed because they do it properly, and for no other reason.

- b-accounting.com, accountants
- cleaningbros.uk, cleaning
- manchesterdental.co.uk, dentists
- crselectricians.co.uk, electricians
- cblofts.co.uk, home improvement
- hangitservices.co.uk, it support
- ybmortgages.co.uk, mortgage and financial advice
- jgpestcontrol.co.uk, pest control
- c1boilers.co.uk, plumbing and heating
- ag-osteopathy.com, private healthcare and physiotherapy
- jamstorage.com, removals
- blueskyguttering.co.uk, roofing
- ayjsolicitors.com, solicitors

## What this means if you are paying for Google Ads

- Ask one question of whoever runs your account. Which conversion action is the primary one, and when did it last record a conversion. If the answer takes more than a minute, read what to check when conversions are not tracking.

- A phone number on the page is not a measured phone call. 80% of these sites show a number and 53% of those have nothing to count the call that follows the click.

- Analytics is not conversion tracking. Google Analytics tells you people came. Only a conversion sent to Google Ads, or imported into it, tells the bidding which clicks were worth paying for.

- Consent handling is part of measurement. A banner that blocks tags with no consent mode behind it removes a share of your conversions from the reports. Google explains how consent mode recovers part of them.

- If your site is in the last group, the first job is not a new campaign. It is a tag, a conversion action and a test. That is what a conversion tracking setup covers, and a PPC audit will tell you which group your own site is in.

## How this was measured

- Finding the advertisers. On 13 November 2026 we searched Google's Ads Transparency Center, with the region set to the United Kingdom, for the words a business in each of 15 service sectors is likely to have in its web address, such as plumbers, solicitors, dental or removals, alone and combined with London, Manchester, Birmingham, Leeds and Bristol. The Transparency Center returns advertiser websites that match.

- Keeping only live advertisers. We checked 420 of those websites in the Transparency Center and kept the 301 with an advert last shown in the UK on or after 14 October 2026.

- Reading the sites. We read the source of each home page, every Google Tag Manager container and Google tag file it refers to, and, for sites built on Wix, the list of tags the platform loads. 277 home pages could be read. The rest refused the request or did not answer.

- Removing what did not belong. We removed sites that were not UK businesses, were not in the sector they were found under, or were parked pages. 230 sites remain.

- Counting. Each share on this page is a count over those 230 sites, or over the sites of one sector. Nothing was estimated or weighted.

### What this study cannot see

- Tags on other pages. Only the home page was read. A conversion tag placed only on a thank-you page is missed, which is why sites with a Google Ads tag and no visible conversion are reported as their own group.

- Imports from Analytics. A business can import results from Google Analytics into Google Ads with no Google Ads tag on the site. That is invisible from outside, so the analytics-only group is not described as untracked.

- Calls counted inside the advert. Calls made straight from a call asset need no tag on the site.

- Tags loaded by a script. The pages were read without running their scripts and without accepting cookies. Where a page showed signs of a tag whose ID we could not read, it was counted in a separate group.

- The sample is not random. Looking for trade words in web addresses favours smaller local firms whose address names what they do. Large national brands are mostly absent.

- Small groups. Sectors hold between 7 and 20 sites, and the reading was taken on a single day.

An earlier edition of this page, published on 6 November 2026, covered 34 sites. This edition replaces it. The larger sample and the reading of Google tag files and Wix tag lists explain the differences between the two.

- https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722022?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10000067?hl=en-GB

### FAQ

**How many UK businesses advertising on Google have conversion tracking?** Of the 230 UK advertisers read for this study, 43% show a Google Ads conversion tag on the home page or inside their tag container. A further 13% carry a Google Ads tag with no conversion action visible from the home page, and 14% show no measurement of any kind.

**Does a Google Analytics tag count as Google Ads conversion tracking?** No. Google Analytics counts visits and events. Google Ads only learns which click became an enquiry when a conversion action is set up in Google Ads or imported from Analytics. In this study 21% of sites had Analytics or a Google tag and no Google Ads tag at all.

**Which UK sectors measure their Google Ads best?** Among the 15 sectors read, mortgage and financial advice had the highest share of sites with a Google Ads conversion tag, at 69%, and cleaning the lowest, at 12%. The groups are small, so the order should be read as a picture and not as a ranking.

**How did you find the advertisers?** Through Google's Ads Transparency Center, with the region set to the United Kingdom. We searched for trade words that appear in web addresses, kept the websites with an advert last shown in the UK in the previous 30 days, and removed those that were not UK businesses in the sector. All 230 are marked as verified advertisers.

**Can a business count phone calls with no tag on its site?** Partly. Google's help page says some conversion measurement does not require a tag, and gives calls from call assets as the example. That counts calls made straight from the advert. It does not count the visitor who clicks through, reads the page and rings the number on it, which needs a call conversion or a call tracking service on the site.

**What should I do if my site has no tag?** Ask whoever runs the account to show you the Conversions page in Google Ads and the status of each action. If there is no action, or it is inactive, the tag needs to be installed and tested before any bidding strategy can work.

## Google Ads Conversions Not Tracking: 6 Checks That Find the Fault

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/guides/google-ads-conversions-not-tracking-uk/
Description: Google Ads conversions not tracking? What Unverified, Tag inactive and No recent conversions mean, six checks an owner can ask for, and why bidding breaks.

Google Ads shows one of a handful of status strings on the Conversions page, and each one separates two very different problems: nothing happened, or nothing was measured. A dead tag, a consent banner that blocks it, a thank-you page that moved, or a GA4 key event that was never imported all produce the same empty column. The checks below can be asked for without logging in, and the last section explains why a campaign on Smart Bidding gets worse, not just blind, when its conversions stop arriving.

Messages this guide covers: Unverified, No recent conversions, Recording conversions, Tag inactive, Inactive, Active, Needs attention, Misconfigured.

## The status strings on the Conversions page, in Google's words

Google has used two generations of labels on the conversion actions table, and both are still documented on its help pages, so you may meet either depending on how your account is laid out. The older per-action tracking statuses are defined on Google's conversion tracking status page. The newer overview statuses are defined in Google's conversion tracking troubleshooter.

| Status | Google's definition | Happened or measured? | What to ask for |

| Unverified | "We haven't verified that your tag has been put on your website yet." | Nothing measured yet. Normal for a few hours after set-up. | A Tag Assistant test of the thank-you page. Google's troubleshooting page treats Unverified lasting more than 24 hours as a problem. |

| No recent conversions | "We've seen your conversion tracking tag, but haven't recorded any conversions over the last seven days." | Tag is alive. Possibly nothing happened, possibly the trigger never fires. | Your own count of enquiries for the same seven days. If you had some, the trigger is wrong. |

| Recording conversions | "We've seen your conversion tag and recorded conversions over the last seven days." | Measured. Check the count against your inbox anyway. | The conversion count by action, to reconcile. |

| Tag inactive | "We can no longer see your tag, and haven't recorded any conversions over the last seven days." | Not measured. The tag was there and has gone. | The date the tag was last seen (hover on the status) and what changed on the website that day. |

| Inactive | Google's conversion measurement page says a new tag may show "Unverified" or "Inactive" and becomes "Active" after the first recorded conversion or a successful test event. | Not measured yet. | A successful test event through Tag Assistant. |

| Active | "indicates that everything is working as intended." | Measured. | Nothing, beyond the monthly reconciliation. |

| Needs attention | "action items to address but that haven't stopped recording conversions entirely." | Partly measured. | The list of alerts behind the status. |

| Misconfigured | "Conversions have stopped recording entirely due to a setup error or a broken tag." | Not measured. | The steps shown when hovering the status, and who will do them by when. |

| Awaiting conversions | "No conversions have been recorded in the last seven days." | Unclear. Google says this typically means the action is under 48 hours old, campaigns are paused or traffic is too low. | The age of the action and whether campaigns are live. |

The column that matters to an owner is the third one. "Nothing happened" is a marketing problem. "Nothing measured" is a plumbing problem, and no change to keywords, ads or budget will fix plumbing.

## "No conversions happened" versus "nothing was measured"

The quickest separation is a reconciliation that needs no access to Google Ads at all. Count the enquiries your business received from the website in the last seven days, from your inbox, phone system or CRM. Then compare with the conversion count in the account for the same seven days, remembering that Google's conversion data page says reporting lags can take 24 to 48 hours and that the main columns are dated by the click, not by the day the enquiry arrived.

- Inbox has enquiries, Google Ads has zero. Nothing was measured. The tag is dead, blocked or on the wrong page.

- Inbox has enquiries, Google Ads has far more. The wrong things are being counted, usually page views, button clicks or a GA4 event that fires on every visit.

- Both have zero. Nothing happened. Check that campaigns are live and that the ads are showing before blaming the tag.

- Roughly the same, within the lag. Measured. Google's page says a discrepancy of up to 20 percent against third-party tools is expected when comparing by conversion time.

Most "conversions not tracking" tickets I see are the first case, and most of those trace to a website change nobody told the account manager about.

## Six checks an owner can ask for

You do not need to run these yourself. You need to ask for them by name and expect a screenshot or a sentence back for each.

- Tag Assistant on the thank-you page. Google's Tag Assistant connects to your site and shows the hits sent and any errors while you click through, and Google's troubleshooting guide for Unverified, Tag inactive and Needs attention actions walks through it: connect, trigger the conversion on the site, close the tool, and the status updates in roughly 30 minutes.

- Tag Manager preview. If the tag lives in Google Tag Manager, preview mode lists the tags that fired on the page and the tags present that did not fire for each event. A conversion tag sitting in the second list on the thank-you page is the fault, found.

- The thank-you page itself. Open it. Website redesigns rename /thank-you to /thanks, forms switch to an on-page success message with no new URL, or a booking tool opens in a frame on another domain. The trigger was written for the old behaviour and never fires again.

- The cookie banner. UK sites need consent before setting non-essential cookies under PECR and UK GDPR, and most consent banners block Google tags until the visitor accepts. If the Google Ads conversion tag is blocked by the banner and nothing else is configured, every visitor who ignores or declines the banner converts invisibly. The next section covers how consent mode changes this.

- GA4 key events versus Google Ads conversions. Many UK accounts measure in GA4 and assume Google Ads sees the same thing. It does not, unless the key event has been created as a Google Ads conversion. Google's conversions versus key events page describes the chain as Event, then Key Event, then Conversion, with a linked Google Ads account required. Its import page lists the prerequisites: the accounts linked, auto-tagging on, and editor rights on the property.

- Offline conversion import. If enquiries are qualified in a CRM and uploaded back, Google's offline conversion import page explains that each click carries a GCLID that must be stored with the lead and sent back when it converts. The conversion measurement page adds that uploads take 24 to 48 hours to process and that the GCLID must be within 90 days of the click. A CRM that stopped storing the GCLID looks exactly like a campaign that stopped converting.

Each of these is a yes or no. A supplier who cannot give you six quick answers is telling you the measurement has not been looked at, which is also the first thing a PPC audit checks before any opinion is offered on the campaigns.

## Cookie consent, PECR and consent mode on UK sites

This is the UK-specific failure. A compliant cookie banner is not optional for a UK business, and the Information Commissioner's Office enforces the rules under PECR alongside UK GDPR. The side effect for measurement is that a banner which simply blocks all Google tags until acceptance makes a share of your real enquiries disappear from Google Ads, and the share is whatever proportion of visitors never click accept.

Google's answer is consent mode, documented on its consent mode page. In basic consent mode, Google tags are blocked until the visitor interacts with the banner and nothing at all is sent when they decline. In advanced consent mode, tags load when the page opens, send cookieless pings while consent is denied, and send full data once consent is granted. Google uses the pings to model conversions it cannot observe, and the page says impact figures appear after consent mode has been live for at least seven full days. Google Tag Manager's consent mode support page lists the consent types and notes that ad_user_data is required for enhanced conversions and tag-based conversion tracking. A banner that grants ad_storage but never sets ad_user_data is a common reason conversions vanish after a consent platform update.

For an owner, the questions are: does our banner integrate with consent mode, basic or advanced, and did anyone test a conversion after declining the banner? If the answer to the second is no, nobody knows what the declined share looks like in your reports. This work sits inside the conversion tracking build rather than being left to whoever installed the banner.

## Why bidding goes wrong when the tag dies

A dead tag is not only a reporting problem. If the campaign uses Smart Bidding, the tag is the steering wheel. Google's Smart Bidding page says Target CPA, Target ROAS, Maximise conversions and Maximise conversion value optimise for conversions in every auction and that conversion tracking must be enabled before you create one. Google recommends judging them over periods with at least 30 conversions, and around 50 for Target ROAS.

Take away the conversions and three things follow. First, the strategy keeps bidding on its last good data, which ages by the day, so it buys clicks that resembled converters in a different month. Second, Google's campaign statuses page notes that "Eligible (misconfigured)" usually means no biddable conversions were recorded in the last 28 days, and its bid strategy statuses page describes "Misconfigured" as a conversion-based strategy without the right conversion actions set up. Third, when the tag is fixed, Google's Smart Bidding learning page says a significant change to the conversion goals being optimised puts the strategy into Learning, which never lasts more than seven days, and performance should then be judged over two conversion cycles or two weeks, whichever is longer.

The reverse failure is worse. If the tag counts page views or every form field click as a conversion, Smart Bidding will dutifully find the visitors most likely to view pages, and the account will report a wonderful cost per conversion while the phone stays silent. That is why I treat "which actions are primary" as the first question in every account, and why the landing pages I build carry a single, deliberate conversion event rather than whatever the website builder emits.

## What to do today, and what not to do

- Reconcile. Seven days of inbox enquiries against seven days of conversions. Decide whether this is "nothing happened" or "nothing measured".

- Read the status and the date the tag was last seen. Match that date against website changes, plugin updates and consent banner changes.

- Test one conversion through Tag Assistant or Tag Manager preview, once with the banner accepted and once declined.

- Check the primary actions. Anything that is not an enquiry becomes secondary so bidding stops chasing it.

- Protect the bidding while you fix the tag. Do not raise budgets or change targets on a strategy that cannot see conversions, and expect up to seven days of Learning after the goal is corrected.

- Do not delete and recreate the conversion action. Google's troubleshooting page says actions with no recorded data for 13 months are removed anyway, and recreating one loses the history that the bidding and your reports depend on.

## Keeping the measurement honest

- Reconcile conversions against the inbox or CRM monthly, and keep the two numbers in the same report.

- Tell whoever runs the account before any website, form, booking tool or consent banner change, and test one conversion the same day it goes live.

- Keep one primary conversion per real business outcome and demote everything else to secondary.

- Store the GCLID in the CRM from the first day you run ads, even if you do not import offline conversions yet.

- Check the Conversions page status weekly. "Tag inactive" noticed on day two costs a fortnight less than "Tag inactive" noticed at month end.

- https://support.google.com/google-ads/troubleshooter/13455130?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/11198131?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10989978?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722022?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6270625?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/tagassistant/answer/10039345?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/tagmanager/answer/6107056?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/13965727?hl=en-GB
- https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/10632359?hl=en-GB

### FAQ

**Why are my Google Ads conversions not showing?** Either nothing happened or nothing was measured. Compare the enquiries in your inbox for the last seven days with the conversions in the account, allowing for Google's stated 24 to 48 hour reporting lag. If the inbox has enquiries and the account has none, the tag is dead, blocked by the cookie banner or firing on a page that no longer exists.

**What does Tag inactive mean in Google Ads?** Google's definition is that it can no longer see your tag and has not recorded any conversions over the last seven days. The tag was there and has gone, usually after a website redesign, a plugin update or a consent banner change. Hover over the status to see the date it was last seen and match that against what changed.

**How long does Google Ads take to verify a conversion tag?** Google says the Unverified check takes a few hours and treats an Unverified status lasting more than 24 hours as a problem to troubleshoot. After a Tag Assistant test, Google says the status updates in roughly 30 minutes. Awaiting conversions on a brand new action typically means it is under 48 hours old.

**Do GA4 key events count as Google Ads conversions?** Not automatically. Google describes the chain as Event, then Key Event, then Conversion, and the key event only becomes a Google Ads conversion once the accounts are linked, auto-tagging is on and the key event has been created as a conversion. An account that only measures in GA4 can show conversions there and nothing in Google Ads.

**Why did performance get worse after the conversion tag broke?** Smart Bidding strategies optimise towards the conversions they can see. With none arriving, the strategy keeps bidding on stale data, the campaign can show Misconfigured, and when the goal is corrected the strategy re-enters Learning, which Google says never lasts more than seven days. Fix the tag before touching budgets or targets.

## How Much Does Google Ads Cost in the UK? 42 Searches Priced

URL: https://ppcconsultancy.uk/guides/google-ads-cost-uk/
Description: Google Ads cost in the UK: how a click is priced, top of page bids for 42 UK searches from Google's own data, and how a daily budget becomes a monthly bill.

Google Ads has no price list. You set an average daily budget, you pay when someone clicks, and the price of each click is set in an auction that runs every time a person searches. That is why one business pays 20p a click and another pays £50. This guide explains how the price is set, shows what Google's own planning data says about 42 UK searches, and works through how a daily budget turns into the amount on the monthly invoice.

Messages this guide covers: Average daily budget, Actual CPC, Top of page bid (low range), Top of page bid (high range), UK DST Fee.

## How Google sets the price of a click

You tell Google the most you are willing to pay for a click, or let an automated bid strategy decide. What you are charged is usually lower. Google's definition of actual cost per click says it is "the final amount that you're charged for a click", and that "you only pay what's minimally required to clear the Ad Rank thresholds and beat the Ad Rank of the competitor immediately below you".

Ad Rank is what decides whether your advert shows and where. Google's Ad Rank page says the values are "calculated based on several factors, including your competition, the context of the person's search and your ad quality at that moment". The context includes the person's location, the device and the time of the search. So the same keyword does not have one price. It has a different price in Leeds and in London, on a phone and on a desktop, at 9am and at midnight.

Quality matters to the price as well as the bid. Google's Quality Score page describes a score "measured on a scale from 1–10" built from three parts: expected click-through rate, ad relevance and landing page experience. The same page is clear that "Quality Score isn't an input in the ad auction". It is a diagnostic. What enters the auction is the quality of the advert and the page at that moment, and an advert that matches the search and leads to a useful page can win a position for less than a competitor who simply bids more.

## What 42 UK searches cost at the top of the page

Google's Keyword Planner shows two columns for every search: "Top of page bid (low range)" and "Top of page bid (high range)". They are estimates of what it takes to appear at the top of the results, not the price of every click. Google's Keyword Planner page gives the example of looking for "keyword ideas where bids under £1 may be enough to reach the top of the page", and adds that "campaign performance depends on a variety of factors".

The table below holds those two columns for 42 searches, for the whole of the United Kingdom, read from Google Ads keyword planning data on 12 November 2026. The data is supplied in US dollars and has been converted at HMRC's monthly exchange rate for November 2026, which is 1.3396 dollars to the pound. Amounts under £10 are rounded to the nearest 10p and larger amounts to the nearest pound.

| Search | Average monthly searches, UK | Top of page bid, low range | Top of page bid, high range |

| Trades and home services |

| emergency plumber | 9,900 | £5.30 | £28 |

| boiler repair | 4,400 | £3.20 | £13 |

| boiler installation | 4,400 | £5.40 | £17 |

| electrician near me | 74,000 | £1.30 | £7.30 |

| locksmith near me | 74,000 | £5.00 | £21 |

| roofer near me | 33,100 | £3.30 | £15 |

| drain unblocking | 27,100 | £2.70 | £14 |

| pest control | 18,100 | £1.90 | £6.50 |

| removals company | 4,400 | £5.40 | £10 |

| loft conversion | 12,100 | £1.30 | £5.90 |

| carpet cleaning | 135,000 | £0.40 | £1.90 |

| Legal and financial services |

| financial adviser | 3,600 | £7.00 | £32 |

| Health and care |

| dental implants | 18,100 | £1.50 | £7.00 |

| invisalign | 90,500 | £2.10 | £8.80 |

| private gp | 8,100 | £2.20 | £8.20 |

| physiotherapy near me | 60,500 | £1.00 | £4.50 |

| laser eye surgery | 27,100 | £3.70 | £11 |

| care home | 40,500 | £1.70 | £8.20 |

| Business services and software |

| it support | 6,600 | £8.30 | £38 |

| managed it services | 1,900 | £9.90 | £35 |

| crm software | 8,100 | £3.30 | £23 |

| accounting software | 6,600 | £17 | £90 |

| hr software | 2,400 | £30 | £123 |

| office cleaning | 1,600 | £2.90 | £22 |

| web design | 12,100 | £2.70 | £11 |

| Retail and consumer |

| sofas | 246,000 | £0.60 | £2.00 |

| mattress | 135,000 | £0.90 | £4.10 |

| engagement rings | 201,000 | £0.90 | £2.70 |

| running shoes | 74,000 | £0.20 | £0.60 |

| garden furniture | 201,000 | £0.20 | £1.20 |

| flowers delivery | 135,000 | £1.90 | £3.90 |

| car leasing | 74,000 | £0.50 | £1.70 |

| driving lessons | 27,100 | £0.50 | £1.80 |

Three things stand out. First, the spread is wide: running shoes sits between 20p and 60p, while HR software sits between £30 and £123. Second, the price follows the value of a customer, not the number of searches. Dentist near me has more than a hundred times the searches of personal injury solicitor and a fraction of the price. Third, within one trade the urgent search costs more. Emergency plumber reaches £28 at the high end, boiler repair £13.

These are national figures for a single phrase. A campaign uses many phrases, usually in one area, and the real average will differ. Treat the table as a way to judge the order of magnitude before you spend, not as a quote.

## From a daily budget to a monthly bill

Google works in days. Its average daily budget page describes the budget as "how much you're roughly comfortable spending each day over the course of the month", and warns that "on some days you might not reach your average daily budget, and on others you might exceed it". Two limits apply. On any one day you will not pay more than "two times your average daily budget for most campaigns". In any one month you will not pay more than "30.4 times your average daily budget for most campaigns".

A worked example, using round numbers:

- You want about 10 clicks a day on searches that cost about £5 each. That is an average daily budget of £50.

- The most Google can charge for that campaign in a month is 30.4 times £50, which is £1,520.

- On a busy day the campaign may spend up to £100. On a quiet day it may spend less than £50. The monthly limit still holds.

- For adverts served in the United Kingdom, Google adds a 2% fee on top, which on £1,520 is £30.40.

The 2% is the UK DST Fee. Google's surcharges page says "a 2% UK DST Fee will be added to your next invoice or statement for ads served in the United Kingdom". It is not included in the campaign budget, so a budget of £1,520 produces a document of about £1,550. VAT is a separate matter again, and for a UK business it is normally handled under the reverse charge. Both are explained in the guide to the Google Ads invoice and VAT.

## How many clicks you need is the real question

The price of a click only means something next to what a click produces. The arithmetic is short:

- Cost per enquiry is the cost of a click divided by the share of visitors who enquire. At £5 a click, with one visitor in twenty enquiring, an enquiry costs £100.

- Cost per customer is the cost per enquiry divided by the share of enquiries that become customers. If one enquiry in four becomes a customer, a customer costs £400.

- Whether that is worth it depends on what a customer is worth to you over time, which only your own books can say.

The numbers in that example are illustrations, not benchmarks. The point is that there are three levers, and only the first is the click price. A landing page that turns one visitor in ten into an enquiry halves the cost per customer without touching a bid. That is why conversion tracking comes before any decision on budget: without it, you know what you paid and not what you got.

## What pushes the cost up, and what brings it down

| What you see | What it usually means | What to do |

| Clicks cost more than the table suggests | You are in a city or a niche with more competition than the national figure, or the advert and page are judged less relevant than a competitor's | Check the search terms that triggered the adverts and the Quality Score parts for the main keywords |

| The budget is gone by lunchtime | The daily budget is small next to the click price, so a few clicks use it up | Narrow the area, the hours or the keywords before raising the budget |

| Plenty of clicks, few enquiries | Broad keywords are matching searches that were never going to buy, or the page does not answer the search | Read the guide to Google Ads that are not working |

| The invoice is higher than the campaign spend | The 2% UK DST Fee and the way charges fall across months | Read the guide to the invoice and VAT |

Google's own bid and budget page puts the trade-off plainly: "With higher bids, your campaign is likely to receive more traffic, although you'll likely spend more money."

## What to do today

- Find your own searches in Keyword Planner. It is inside Google Ads under Tools. Set the location to your town or region, not the whole country, and note the two top of page bid columns.

- Decide what a customer is worth. Not the first sale only. What the customer brings over a year or two, at your margin.

- Work backwards to a daily budget. Clicks needed for one enquiry, enquiries needed for one customer, and the click price from step one. Multiply the daily figure by 30.4 for the monthly limit.

- Add 2% for the UK DST Fee. And ask your accountant how the reverse charge applies to you.

- Set up conversion tracking before the first click. So that the first month tells you a cost per enquiry and not only a cost per click.

- Keep the two costs apart. What you pay Google for clicks is one thing. What you pay someone to run the account is another, and it is covered on the pricing page. If you would like the numbers checked before you commit a budget, that is what a PPC consultation is for.
